legend: The plasmablasts, based on immunostaining for latency-associated nuclear antigen (LANA; ORF73), are infected with KSHV/HHV8; this KSHV/HHV8 gene product tethers the virus to the human DNA (<<31275>>). At higher magnification, immunostaining for LANA in the KSHV/HHV8-infected cells shows a characteristic nuclear-dot pattern (<<31276>>). A significant number of the LANA-positive plasmablasts also express vIL-6 (<<31277>>).

Large groups of plasmablasts can be seen in KSHV/HHV8-associated multicentric Castleman disease (<<31541>>). The plasmablast aggregates are composed of KSHV/HHV8-positive cells, as demonstrated by immunostaining for latency-associated nuclear antigen (LANA) (immunoperoxidase staining) (<<31542>>). Plasmablasts are polyclonal according to IG gene rearrangement studies, but at the protein level are lambda immunoglobulin light chain monotypic, as demonstrated by double immunostaining for LANA (brown) and kappa or lambda immunoglobulin light chain (red), in which the KSHV/HHV8-positive cells are kappa light chain–negative (immunoperoxidase staining, LANA, and streptavidin, kappa light chain) (<<31281>>) but lambda light chain–positive (immunoperoxidase staining, LANA, and streptavidin, lambda light chain) (<<31282>>).
